questionText: An example of a compound is
explanation: Sand (silicate IV oxide) is a compound; milk, blood, and air are mixtures.

questionText: Which of the following orbitals has zero-fold degeneracy?
explanation: The \(s\)-orbital has zero-fold degeneracy — only one orientation exists.

questionText: The molecular lattice of iodine is held together by
explanation: Iodine and naphthalene molecular lattices are held by weak van der Waal's forces.

questionText: What volume of unused \(\text{H}_2\) remains when \(100\,\text{cm}^3\) of \(\text{H}_2\) is burnt in \(40\,\text{cm}^3\) of \(\text{O}_2\)? \[2\text{H}_2(g)+\text{O}_2(g)\rightarrow2\text{H}_2\text{O}(g)\]
What is the percentage of sulphur in sulphur(IV) oxide? \([\text{S}=32,\;\text{O}=16]\)
A solubility graph shows curves A, B, C, D vs temperature. The salt whose solubility is independent of temperature is
explanation: Curve C is flat (horizontal), showing solubility independent of temperature.

questionText: If the heat of combustion of hydrogen is \(-285.8\,\text{kJ}\), what is the heat of formation of water?
explanation: The combustion of \(\text{H}_2\) forms \(\text{H}_2\text{O}\), so the heat of combustion equals the heat of formation: \(-285.8\,\text{kJ}\)

questionText: \(\text{N}_2\text{O}_4(g)\rightleftharpoons2\text{NO}_2(g)\). More product formation is favoured by
explanation: Decreasing pressure favours the side with more moles of gas — the product side (2 mol \(\text{NO}_2\)).

questionText: The oxidation state of carbon in COOH is
explanation: In the carboxyl group (–COOH), assigning oxidation states gives carbon a value of \(+2\).

explanation: Litmus appears purple in a neutral medium.

questionText: The air around a petroleum refinery most likely contains
explanation: Fossil fuel pollution from refineries includes \(\text{SO}_2\), CO and \(\text{NO}_2\).

questionText: The monomeric unit of natural rubber is
explanation: Isoprene (2-methylbuta-1,3-diene) is the monomer of natural rubber.

questionText: What property makes duralumin more useful than its constituent metals?

options.A: it is heavy with a high melting point
options.B: it is malleable and has high density

explanation: Duralumin is valued for being both strong and light — ideal for aircraft construction.
